_comment: The audit trail. Every figure that was checked against a live source, with the sentence that was read back off it; and every claim that failed checking, with why. This is the proof file's raw material - analysis/export_evidence.py turns it plus species/species.json into the Excel workbook.

verified.claim: Hong Kong Bird Report 1958-2014 is freely downloadable
verified.quote: Index lists every year 1958-1998 individually then multi-year volumes to 2014. HTTP 200 confirmed for 1970-71 (22MB), 1972 (15MB), 1973 (12MB), 1974 (18MB), 1979 (11MB), 1991 (31MB) at /web/chi/documents/bird_report/<YEAR>_birdreport_protected.pdf

rejected.claim: Deep Bay mid-winter waterbird totals, annual 1979-2024 (13,200 rising to 53,200 by 1995, peak 90,100 in 2008)
rejected.origin: Kimi compiled workbook, sheet 'Deep Bay Mid-Winter Waterbirds'
rejected.reason: The 1979-1995 run rises monotonically for seventeen consecutive years, and every guild sub-column does the same. Real waterbird counts swing with weather, tides and observer effort; nothing in nature is that smooth. It also conflicts with three other figures: a separate pass gives 48,784 for January 1991 against this table's 41,500, and HKBWS annual reports give 55,509 / 56,354 / 65,000 for 2015-16 / 2016-17 / 2017-18 against this table's 57,200 / 54,500 / 52,800. Treated as generated, not observed.

rejected.claim: Black-faced Spoonbill Deep Bay counts 1975-1993 (12 rising smoothly to 72)
rejected.reason: Near-monotonic ramp across nineteen years. The same sheet dates the first International Synchronous Census to 1994, so these pre-census figures would have to come from individual Bird Reports, which are not cited beyond a generic 'HKBR <year>'. Plausible in magnitude, unusable as evidence. The Bird Report archive is now known to be reachable, so these years can be settled properly.

rejected.claim: Decade peak counts per species, e.g. Northern Pintail 1990s peak 4,100; Common Shelduck 1980s 1,400; Eurasian Coot 2010s 290 and 2020s 140
rejected.origin: Kimi compiled workbook, sheet 'Key Species Population Trends'
rejected.reason: Directly contradicts figures verified from HKBWS the same day. Pintail's verified 1997 count is 8,651, more than double the claimed 1990s peak. Shelduck's verified 1988 peak is 4,011 against a claimed 1980s baseline of 1,400. Coot's verified ceiling since 2011/12 is 66, against claimed 290 and 140. Where a compiled figure and a primary source disagree, the primary source wins.

rejected.claim: Long Valley annual species totals (130 in 2006 rising to 314 in 2018, then 256 in 2023, then 'over 190' in 2026)
rejected.reason: Internally inconsistent - a series cannot rise to 314 and then fall to 190 on the same basis. Almost certainly mixes a cumulative all-time species list with per-year counts. Species richness is not abundance and would not be usable here in any case.

rejected.origin: Widely cited 1998-2017 Deep Bay trend study
rejected.reason: The study's window simply ends in 2017. The HKBWS account records a later bird, present 26 February to 18 March 2020.

rejected.claim: White-throated Kingfisher breeding occupancy fell 21.9% to 5.4%
rejected.origin: Secondary summary supplied at project start
rejected.reason: The primary account gives 7.3% to 3.0% for breeding and 9.4% to 5.7% for winter. The larger figures are not supported by it.

rejected.claim: Black-faced Spoonbill Deep Bay peak of 411 in 2016
rejected.origin: My own earlier inference from the 2026 report's phrase 'the peak of 411 recorded ten years ago'
rejected.reason: The number 411 is real but the year was inferred from a loose phrase. Two independent compiled series put 371 in 2016 and 411 in 2011 and 2015, and the 2011 reading is corroborated by ratio against the 2024 report's 'over 20% in 2011'. My inference is withdrawn.

rejected.claim: All Hong Kong Bird Reports 1958-2012 are online
rejected.reason: Wrong as stated - the current CMS page lists 1993-2018 only. But the legacy index does carry 1958-2014, so the underlying recommendation was right and better than the claim. Recorded here because the reasoning mattered more than the wording.

rejected.claim: Every figure in the Chinese-language research pass
rejected.reason: Returned with no source URLs at all, despite the sourcing requirement. Not rejected as false - several items later proved correct - but nothing from it was allowed into the data on its own authority. Each item was treated as a lead and checked independently.

rejected.origin: My own ranking of 168 Bird Report peak-count tables by first-to-last value
rejected.reason: A ranking cannot see a spike. HKBWS states: 'peak counts are higher than in the 1990s with an exceptional count in 2010'. The apparent collapse is the 2010 outlier falling out of the window. Not a decliner.
HKBWS states: 'relatively stable since the 1990s except for exceptionally high numbers in the winter of 2006-07'. Same spike artefact.
HKBWS lists it among 'species which have increased substantially in numbers since the 1990s and before'. The trend is the opposite of the ranking.
HKBWS states it 'was increasing in numbers up to 2012'.
HKBWS states it 'is now recorded in higher numbers than in the 1990s, mostly at MPNR'.

rejected.claim: Eurasian Skylark and Greater Painted-snipe as decline candidates
rejected.reason: HKBWS states Skylark 'has increased substantially' and Painted-snipe peak counts are 'relatively stable since 1994'.
